name: Ike Fit

classes.doctrine: Fleet-wide rule inherited by every vessel unless explicitly superseded by Admiral governance.
classes.capability: Reusable primitive that must be adapted to mission/users/data/risk before adoption.
classes.mission_adapter: Project-specific implementation; never copied across vessels as-is.

transfer_rule: Learn -> classify -> adapt -> Captain review -> adopt. No business-specific data or branding transfers automatically.

learnings.title: Doctrine Inheritance
learnings.lesson: True fleet doctrine is inherited automatically by every admitted vessel and proven centrally; it must not create repetitive per-vessel review chores.
learnings.missionAdapter: Fleet law applies automatically while vessel-specific implementation evidence remains isolated.

learnings.title: Recommendation Compression
learnings.lesson: Many raw project matches must be compressed into a small number of mission-aware Admiral decisions, with shared deficiencies grouped as fleet patterns.
learnings.missionAdapter: Show the Admiral decisions, not the bookkeeping that produced them.

learnings.title: Mission-Fit Confidence
learnings.lesson: Reusable capabilities must explain why they fit each vessel. Strong fits may be staged together; plausible fits require review; experimental fits are suppressed from bulk staging.
learnings.missionAdapter: Never infer capability fit from a weak proxy such as photo availability alone.

learnings.title: Manufacturability-Aware Composition Fit
learnings.lesson: Treat customer layout as usable-face geometry + scale + optical placement together; preserve the exact source image/material and let each vessel define its own mission-specific fit behavior.

confidence_rubric.strong: Mission evidence directly supports staging; bulk stage may include these matches.
confidence_rubric.plausible: Useful fit, but mission adaptation or authority evidence should be reviewed before staging.
confidence_rubric.experimental: Weak or indirect fit; automatically excluded from bulk staging and surfaced only as suppressed evidence.
